scores.note: Example-app maintenance. Real content for this environment: archApp/bplreport.py is INSTALLED (install/python3.13/linux-x86_64/bplreport.py) and at the pin is Python-2 syntax: 'python3 -m py_compile build-pin/archApp/bplreport.py' -> SyntaxError (print statement); with F1 it compiles and 'import bplreport' succeeds. 'DB += bplstorage.db' makes archApp/bplstorage.db (tracked but not installed at the pin) appear in install/db (verified: build-pin/install/db lacks it, build-F1/install/db has it). disect.py change removes the already-guarded py2 InstanceType block (cosmetic; the #53 fix at the pin already made it safe). Windows .bat files and env_vars.bat are inert on Linux. iocweatherbnl/st.cmd adds inline '#' comments after dbLoadRecords; verified iocsh accepts them (softIoc < comment.cmd, epicsEnvSet with trailing comment gave X=1). Value is limited to the archiver demo, whose endpoint (capp02.cs.nsls2.local) is NSLS-II internal, so the demo cannot run here anyway. Not complete on its own for py3: F2 is still needed for fetch_float/fetch_string to work.

Three genuine py3 defects in the installed archiver demo: (1) str.translate(None, ',') raises TypeError on py3 (verified: python3 -c "str(1234).translate(None, ',')" -> TypeError: str.translate() takes exactly one argument); (2) fetch_string assigned bytes (.encode('ascii')) to a stringin VAL, which the pin's dbfield.c rejects (verified with real records in my probe: rec.VAL = b'xyz' raises TypeError('bad argument type for built-in operation'); str works); (3) bplstorage.db wired ai records to fetch_string, i.e. a str into an ai VAL. All three are fixed. But the file it patches is Python-2 syntax without F1 (build-F2/archApp/bplreport.py still fails py_compile), and bplstorage.db is only installed with F1's Makefile line, so F2 is only meaningful on top of F1. Applies alone with offset -3 (patch -p1 --dry-run rc=0). Example material only; no site code depends on it.

Only one installed file is touched: logApp/src/inotifyy.py (installed as inotifyy.py). Its decodeMask() used dict.iteritems(): verified on the pin install 'import inotifyy; inotifyy.decodeMask(0x300)' -> AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'iteritems'; with F3 -> "0x300 ['CREATE', 'DELETE']". decodeMask is only called from the debug prints in cmdlisten()/cmdtail.direvt(), not from the logwatch/caputlog data path. iocBoot/iocFPM/fpm.py and loadnp.py are not installed (iocBoot is example material, iocFPM needs iocStats/autosave) but they are genuine py3 fixes: print statements (py_compile fails at the pin, passes with F3) and len(raw)/sampPturn -> // (float slice bound would TypeError). The two st.cmd shebangs are changed to a hard-coded ../../bin/linux-x86_64/softIocPy3.6, which is wrong for this environment (softIocPy3.13) just as the old one was. Clean apply, zero regression surface for the module proper.

Behaviour change in devsup.ptable, not a defect fix. Measured with a real Table/records probe (ai get, ao set, ai get; {R}/tests/test_ptable_alarm.py, run per method on build-pin and build-F4, logs {R}/probe-ptable-*). Differences for an existing 2.1.0 user: (a) get records: with P.alarm set and no stat the record still gets STAT=COMM (9) on both, so plain '.alarm' users are unchanged; new P.stat/P.amsg are honoured (pin STAT 9 AMSG '' -> F4 STAT 3 AMSG 'A hihi'). (b) Output ('set') records now receive the table alarm after the record->table write: pin pt:setB SEVR 0 after an action raised MAJOR; F4 SEVR 2 STAT 3 AMSG set. An existing IOC whose actions set P.alarm (e.g. to flag an invalid input) will see its ao/longout records go into alarm after the bump/patch - new, visible on screens and in alarm handlers. (c) Assigning None no longer sets P.alarm to INVALID (pin P.alarm 3, F4 keeps the previous value, here 1); record outcome is the same (INVALID/UDF via the None branch) and isvalid is False on both, but code reading P.alarm after a None assignment changes. (d) Assigning a non-None value clears P.alarm on both (unchanged); F4 does NOT clear P.stat/P.amsg, so a later '.alarm = MINOR' without re-setting stat re-emits the stale HIHI/'A hihi' (s6 in the log). (e) _ParamInstance._get_value/_set_value are removed (property rewritten); hasattr check shows True at the pin, False with F4 - breaks only code that referenced those private names. (f) Unchanged pre-existing pin defect that F4's own comment touches but does not fix: _ParamSupBase.raw = (pyfield != 'RVAL') is True for the default VAL, so process_record2 returns 2 and longin/longout 'get' records never clear UDF (probe_udf.py: longin VAL 5, UDF 1, SEVR 3 STAT 17 on pin and on F4; ai clears UDF). The PR text says the author found this mistaken, but the merged diff keeps it. (g) The four TestAlarmScan tests added by F4 exercise Record.setSevr on plain longin/longout and never touch ptable; the ptable change ships untested by its own PR. Shipped tests: 15 pass on pin+F4. Applies cleanly; file-overlap with F5 on test_db.py in both orders. Locality is medium: ptable.py is a library module that site IOC Python imports. Value for the facility exists (alarm message on parameter records) but carrying a behaviour change with stale-message semantics ahead of the release is not compelling.

Real use-after-free in the shipped unit-test harness, reproduced on the pin without stubs: testdbCleanup() frees every record but devsup.db._rec_cache keeps Record objects whose DBENTRY precnode now dangles. (1) My probe {R}/tests/test_rec_cache.py (two IOCHelper cases that both load a record named reuse:x) -> on build-pin: 'Segmentation fault' (rc=139) in the second case; on build-F5: both pass, second getRecord returns a fresh object (RTYP ai, VAL 2.5). (2) F5's own new tests run against the pin's unchanged util.py (writable copy of the F5 install with pin util.py, {R}/f5-nocache2): test_aao_float and test_aao_long FAIL (stale object, wrong values), 14 others pass; with the F5 util.py all 16 pass. (3) My F4 ptable probe, which reuses record names across methods, segfaulted on build-pin and build-F4 and ran on build-all. The pin's own suite never reuses a name, which is why 11 tests pass there. Scope is the test harness (IOCHelper.tearDown) plus a clearer AttributeError text in db.py ('No such field ' + name) and new aai/aao/wf-long tests; production IOCs never free records, so running IOCs are unaffected, which caps ops/urgency. Site modules that use devsup.test.util.IOCHelper in their own CI benefit directly. Clean apply (singly and after F4; F4 also applies after F5 with offset 98).

More than a deprecation cleanup on this Base. libCom.so of the installed 7.0.10 contains 'epicsThreadExitMain() must no longer be used.' (strings), and the epics-base source at R7.0.10 calls cantProceed() first thing in epicsThreadExitMain(). defects.description: Stale alarm context: assigning a non-None value clears P.alarm but leaves P.stat and P.amsg; a later P.alarm = MINOR without re-setting stat re-emits the old HIHI status and old message on the record (probe s6: F4 STAT 3 AMSG 'A hihi' for a MINOR alarm raised after the HIHI alarm had been cleared; pin gives STAT COMM, no message).

Behaviour change not mentioned as such: output ('set') records now receive the parameter alarm (rec.setSevr after the record->table write). An existing IOC whose actions raise P.alarm will see its ao/longout records go into alarm (probe t2: pin pt:setB SEVR 0, F4 SEVR 2 STAT 3 AMSG 'B too large'). Assigning None no longer sets P.alarm = INVALID_ALARM (pin 3, F4 keeps the previous value); the record still gets INVALID/UDF via the None branch, but code that reads P.alarm after a None assignment changes. _ParamInstance._get_value/_set_value are removed.

The PR's own tests (TestAlarmScan) only call Record.setSevr on plain longin/longout and scan them; nothing in the added tests instantiates a ptable TableBase or a '@devsup.ptable' link, so the ptable.py change ships untested. The added comment on self.raw describes it as 'rawsupport' although raw is True for the default pyfield VAL, which makes process_record2 return 2 and leaves longin get records in UDF alarm (pre-existing, measured on pin and F4, not fixed by F4 despite the PR discussion saying it would be). Diff also adds two whitespace-only lines.

Feature plus behaviour change in devsup.ptable, the installed API that site IOC code is written against. Verified by running the real devsup.ptable through IOCHelper on pin and patched builds (r2/ptable-test/test_ptable_r2.py): (1) alarm severity set with a value: pin SEVR=MAJOR STAT=COMM AMSG=''; F4 SEVR=MAJOR STAT=<inst.stat or COMM> AMSG=<inst.amsg> - new stat/amsg attributes work; (2) assigning a non-None value while an alarm is set clears inst.alarm to 0 in both versions (unchanged); (3) assigning None: pin sets inst.alarm=3 (INVALID_ALARM); F4 leaves inst.alarm untouched (observed 2 after MAJOR). The record still gets INVALID/UDF in both versions and isvalid is False in both, so only code that reads _ParamInstance.alarm directly after a None assignment sees a difference; (4) output ('set') records: pin never touched the record alarm in the record-to-table direction; F4 applies inst.alarm/stat/amsg to the output record after the actions run (verified: an onchange action raising MAJOR on the parameter makes the ao record MAJOR/COMM under F4, NO_ALARM on pin). (4) is the behaviour change most likely to surprise a site table that sets .alarm on a set-parameter. Shipped tests: the four TestAlarmScan cases added by the commit pass (15 tests OK), but they only call Record.setSevr on plain longin/longout records without Python device support and do not exercise ptable.py at all, so the commit's own tests give no coverage of the code it changes. Upstream PR #52 review confirms the stat-default and action-order questions were argued out; the merged shape is coherent. Value for this facility: alarm messages on ptable records are useful for validation feedback, but no site code here needs it before the next release. Applies cleanly singly and with the set (no conflict with F5 in either order), but the regression surface is the whole ptable alarm path.

The pin's own 11 shipped tests do not reuse names and pass unpatched, so nothing shipped today crashes; the defect only bites when a test case reuses a record name after testdbCleanup(). It is confined to devsup.test (IOCHelper tearDown) and does not change runtime IOC behaviour: _rec_cache is only cleared in tearDown. db.py change is an error-message improvement ('No such field ' + name). Also broadens coverage (waveform LONG, aai, aao with PP links). Applies cleanly singly and in the set (test_db.py overlaps with F4 but both orders apply, offset only). Worth carrying if the environment runs the shipped tests as its verification gate and wants to extend them; otherwise low urgency.

Behaviour change in the devsup.ptable core API, not a defect fix. The pin's Record.setSevr already accepts stat/amsg; F4 makes ptable carry _ParamInstance.stat/.amsg to records and applies the table alarm on the output (set) path. Characterized on the real built module with my own ptable test (r3/tests/r3_ptable.py, 7 scenarios, run on pin, F4 and all trees): IDENTICAL on pin and F4 -> alarm-only get (SEVR MAJOR, STAT COMM), assigning a non-None value clears the parameter alarm, an alarm set without assignment persists across scans, set path with no action leaves NO_ALARM, setSevr(NO_ALARM,...) after MAJOR is a no-op. CHANGED -> (1) get path honours stat/amsg: pin STAT=COMM AMSG='' vs F4 STAT=HIGH AMSG='hello'; (2) set path: an onproc action raising P.alarm/stat/amsg now puts the output record into alarm (pin SEVR=0, F4 SEVR=MAJOR STAT=HIGH AMSG='bad value'); (3) P.value=None no longer sets P.alarm=INVALID_ALARM (pin alarm=3, F4 alarm=0); (4) P.value=None while P.alarm=MAJOR leaves alarm MAJOR (pin forced 3). The record still gets INVALID/UDF for None on both, and isvalid is unchanged. Site code reading P.alarm after a None assignment, or site tables whose action raises P.alarm for the readback record and did not expect the setpoint (ao/longout) record to alarm too, see different behaviour. Upstream review itself flagged the alarm-clearing semantics change. Shipped TestAlarmScan tests exercise Record.setSevr via scan, not ptable, so the changed code has no upstream test coverage. Clean apply, build OK, tests 15/15 OK. Deepest change of the seven (core module used by site IOC code outside this repository).

Runtime IOC code is unaffected: db.py only gains the field name in the 'No such field' AttributeError message; the cache clear lives in devsup.test.util.IOCHelper.tearDown. Value is for the environment's and site's test runs (any site IOCHelper test reusing record names across cases crashes at the pin). Clean apply, build OK.

The one fix that corrects observable misbehaviour on this environment's Base. Pin softIocPy3.13 built against Base 7.0.10, started non-interactively ('softIocPy3.13 -S -d small.db'): after 'iocRun: All initialization complete' it prints 'epicsThreadExitMain() must no longer be used.' then 'CRITICAL ERROR Thread _main_ (...) can't proceed, suspending.' and dumps a stack trace (libCom cantProceed <- epicsThreadExitMain <- main). The IOC does keep serving (alive after 3 s, SIGTERM exit 143), so it is not fatal, but every unattended start logs a CRITICAL ERROR with a stack trace and leaves the main thread suspended by cantProceed. The F6 tree starts clean ('iocRun: All initialization complete' and nothing else), stays alive, SIGTERM exit 143; the interactive path (st-f7.cmd through iocsh ending with exit) exits 0 on both. Same pattern as Base's own softMain.cpp (epics-base de3cdce 'softIoc: spin to keep alive'). Build on the pin warns 'epicsThreadExitMain() is deprecated'; the F6 build has no such warning. Four-line change confined to pyIocApp/devsupMain.cpp (the softIocPy program), not the _dbapi library; applies and builds cleanly, tests 11/11 OK. Since all six OS targets use Base 7.0.10, every softIocPy -S deployment is affected.

Behaviour change for existing ptable users, observed (r3_ptable.py S5): the set (output record) path now calls rec.setSevr(alarm, stat, amsg) after the actions run. At the pin an output record never carried the table alarm (SEVR 0); with F4 an onproc action that raises P.alarm puts the ao/longout setpoint record itself into alarm (SEVR MAJOR, STAT HIGH, AMSG 'bad value'). Intended by the author, but it changes what 2.1.0 site tables display on their setpoint records.

Inconsistent state in the fix itself: the value setter clears alarm on a non-None assignment but leaves stat and amsg untouched, so a later P.alarm = MAJOR without re-setting stat/amsg re-applies the previous parameter's stat/amsg to the record. Also the PR text says stat is initialised to UDF_ALARM while the code initialises it to None (falls back to COMM_ALARM), and the shipped TestAlarmScan tests exercise Record.setSevr through record scan rather than any ptable code, so the changed module has no upstream test coverage. Adds stat/amsg attributes to ptable parameters and passes them to Record.setSevr on both get and set records. Executed a ptable probe (ai/ao records with '@devsup.ptable probe get/set') against the pin install and the f4 install, one test method per process. Observable differences for an existing 2.1.0 user: (1) assigning None: pin sets P.alarm=3 (INVALID_ALARM), F4 leaves P.alarm at its previous value (probe: alarm after value=None -> 3 on pin, 1 on f4); the attached get record still gets SEVR=3 STAT=17 (INVALID/UDF) on both. (2) assigning a non-None value: both clear alarm to 0 (probe: 0 on both). (3) get record with P.alarm=MINOR and P.stat=HIHI, P.amsg set: pin -> SEVR 1 STAT 9 (COMM) AMSG ''; F4 -> SEVR 1 STAT 3 (HIHI) AMSG 'get-path msg'. (4) set path (ao record whose onproc action sets alarm/stat/amsg): pin never alarms the output record (SEVR 0 STAT 0) although inst.alarm is 2; F4 alarms it (SEVR 2 STAT 3 AMSG 'set-path alarm'). Site code that detects an undefined parameter via P.alarm == INVALID_ALARM instead of P.isvalid would break; code that set P.alarm inside a set-parameter action will now see its output record alarmed; code that monkeypatched the removed private _get_value/_set_value would silently stop working. These are documented upstream under Changed. It is a feature with a behaviour change rather than a fix of a harm, so there is no cost in waiting for the release; moderate regression surface because ptable is the framework site IOC code builds on. Applies cleanly to the pin; shipped tests: 15 pass on f4 (11 on pin). The tests F4 adds (TestAlarmScan) use plain longin/longout records with no DTYP and only exercise Record.setSevr, not ptable.

A feature, not a defect fix, in devsup.ptable, a shipped API that site IOC code uses. Observable changes for a 2.1.0 user, measured by driving the real 'Python Device' dset and devsup.ptable.build on a longin 'get' and a longout 'set' record (mytests/test_ptable_behaviour.py, run per test case against pin, F4 and all7): (1) assigning None no longer sets P.alarm to INVALID: pin P.alarm=3 after P.value=None, F4 leaves it unchanged (0, or 2 when MAJOR had been set before); P.isvalid is still False and the record still gets INVALID/UDF on processing, so only code reading P.alarm directly sees the difference. (2) Assigning a non-None value while an alarm is set clears P.alarm to 0 on both versions (same). (3) New P.stat and P.amsg attributes are honoured on the get path: alarm=MAJOR stat=HIHI amsg -> F4 record SEVR=2 STAT=3 AMSG='table says hihi'; pin SEVR=2 STAT=9 AMSG='' (COMM, message ignored). With no stat set both give STAT=COMM. (4) Output ('set') records now receive rec.setSevr(alarm, stat, amsg) after the parameter actions run: an onproc action that sets self.B.alarm=MINOR makes the longout show SEVR=1 STAT=4 AMSG on F4, SEVR=0 on the pin, where ptable never touched output-record alarms. Site code written against 2.1.0 that sets P.alarm on a parameter bound to a set record will see those output records enter alarm after the carry; code that tests P.alarm >= INVALID_ALARM instead of P.isvalid after assigning None changes meaning. Both are plausible in table code, so the carry is a behaviour change to weigh, not a free fix. Defects in the fix: stat/amsg are never cleared (after alarm clears, stat=3 amsg='table says hihi' persist and are reused by the next plain P.alarm=MAJOR), and the four added TestAlarmScan tests use records with no DTYP, so they test Record.setSevr + scan, not the ptable change at all. Shipped tests: 15/15 OK on F4, 20/20 on all7. Applies cleanly on the pin and after F5 (offset 98 lines).

Fixes a real use-after-free, but only on the unit-test harness path: testdbCleanup() frees every record, devsup.db._rec_cache keeps the Record objects, and the next test case's getRecord() of the same name returns a stale object. Reproduced on the pin with mytests/test_reuse.py (two IOCHelper cases on 'reuse:rec'): first case ok, second case Segmentation fault (nose2 exit 139); with F5 (and all7) both pass. In a running IOC records are never freed, so no runtime IOC behaviour changes; the only non-test change is a clearer AttributeError message in db.py ('No such field ' + name). Value is for anyone writing IOCHelper tests (my own two check modules segfaulted on the pin for this reason, and F4's new tests only avoid it by using unique record names). The added aai/aao/waveform-long tests are useful coverage. Applies cleanly singly and in either order with F4 on test_db.py.

defects.description: P.stat and P.amsg are never reset when the alarm clears: after alarm=MAJOR stat=HIHI amsg='table says hihi' and then P.value=8, the parameter reads alarm=0 stat=3 amsg='table says hihi' (OBS get 5 on F4 and all7; set path OBS set 2 likewise keeps stat=4 and the message). The next plain P.alarm=MAJOR, which is the 2.1.0-era API with no stat argument, therefore reuses the stale HIHI status and message on the record instead of COMM_ALARM with no message. The value setter clears only self.alarm (ptable.py value.setter), so this is in the fix itself.

Behaviour change that can break code written against 2.1.0: (a) 'set' (output) records now receive rec.setSevr(alarm, stat, amsg) on every record-to-table write (OBS set 1: longout SEVR=1 STAT=4 on F4, SEVR=0 on the pin for the same table action), so any site table that sets P.alarm on a parameter bound to an output record puts that record into alarm after the carry; (b) P.value=None no longer sets P.alarm=INVALID_ALARM (pin alarm=3, F4 alarm unchanged, OBS get 2 and get 6), so code that inspects P.alarm rather than P.isvalid after assigning None reads a different value. P.isvalid and the INVALID/UDF put on get records for None are unchanged.

The four TestAlarmScan tests added by the fix do not exercise the change: their records have no DTYP, so they test Record.setSevr followed by scan on soft records and never go through devsup.ptable. The ptable rewrite (value setter, stat/amsg plumbing, new setSevr on the set path) is untested by the shipped suite; verified by reading the test db strings in the diff and by the fact that my ptable-driven checks are the only ones where pin and F4 differ.
